title: Special: Why Does a Venus Flytrap Count Touches?
topic_key: venus flytrap touch counting calcium action potentials
audience_promise: See why a Venus flytrap waits for repeated movement before spending energy to close and digest prey.
wonder_hook: Why does a Venus flytrap wait for two touches before it snaps shut?

age_layers.children: Watch one tiny hair trigger a big plant movement.
age_layers.family: See how the plant avoids wasting energy on one accidental touch.
age_layers.deeper: Follow electrical signals, calcium waves and threshold decisions in a living plant.

science_boundary: The storyboard shows the documented touch, electrical and calcium-signal sequence. It does not claim that the plant thinks or makes a conscious decision.

sources.title: University of Würzburg: How the Venus Flytrap Counts
sources.observation: A prey touching a sensory hair triggers an action potential; two rapid signals overlap as calcium waves and can exceed the threshold for trap closure.

sources.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew: Carnivorous plants explained
sources.observation: The trap generally closes after two hair touches in a short time and begins releasing digestive enzymes only after additional stimulation.

growth_plan.hook_line: A Venus flytrap does not snap at every touch—it counts first.
growth_plan.retention_promise: Each five-second beat reveals why another touch changes what the plant does next.
growth_plan.follow_reason: Follow AION for visual explanations of surprising mechanisms in nature and history.
growth_plan.series_angle: Plant behaviour is explained as a visible sequence of signals, thresholds and energy choices.

reality_anchor.topic: Why a Venus flytrap usually closes after two quick touches
evidence_claims: A touch of a sensory hair triggers an electrical action potential that spreads across the trap.
Two rapid action potentials can overlap as calcium waves and exceed a threshold that closes the trap.
reality_anchor.rule: Depict the trigger hairs, electrical signals, calcium threshold and trap movement before decorative atmosphere.

mechanism_flow: Show one touch and its signal.
Show a second quick signal adding before the first fades.
Show the threshold crossing, closure and later digestion response.

creative_boundary.allowed: Clear symbolic pulses and colour-coded plant cross-sections may make the invisible signals readable.
creative_boundary.prohibited: Do not depict the plant as conscious, talking, thinking, or using human-made electronics.

thumbnail_concept: Open red Venus flytrap with two amber pulse rings landing on one trigger hair; dark cobalt background; no text.

scenes.narration: A Venus flytrap does not snap at every touch. It counts first.
scenes.visual: AION appears small beside one open red Venus flytrap; one trigger hair carries a single amber pulse while the trap remains open.

scenes.narration: Inside each trap are tiny hairs that sense a visitor moving.
scenes.visual: Macro 2D view of two delicate trigger hairs inside the red trap; AION is only a cyan crystal-marker at the edge.

scenes.narration: One bent hair sends an electrical signal across the leaf.
scenes.visual: One hair bends under a small insect foot; a single amber pulse travels through a simplified dark-indigo leaf cross-section; AION marker is tiny.

scenes.narration: But one signal usually is not enough to close the trap.
scenes.visual: Split-simple composition: one fading amber pulse on the left and an open trap on the right; AION marker remains tiny.

scenes.narration: A second quick touch arrives before the first signal disappears.
scenes.visual: Two amber pulses overlap along the same leaf path from two trigger-hair touches; AION marker is small and non-dominant.

scenes.narration: Together they raise a calcium wave inside the trap's cells.
scenes.visual: Clean cellular cutaway: two amber signals become one rising coral-and-cyan calcium wave; AION marker at the lower edge.

scenes.narration: Cross the threshold, and the two leaf lobes snap shut.
scenes.visual: One dominant Venus flytrap changes from open to closed around a small insect; green threshold glow marks the mechanism, with a tiny AION marker.

scenes.narration: More movement tells the plant that real prey is still inside.
scenes.visual: Closed trap shown as a calm cutaway; small repeated amber taps continue inside while AION appears as a tiny contextual guide.

scenes.narration: So it saves energy instead of reacting to every raindrop.
scenes.visual: Comparison of a harmless raindrop outside and a closed trap with a few extra pulses inside; no anthropomorphic plant; AION marker only.

scenes.narration: It uses a tiny biological memory, saving energy for real prey.
scenes.visual: Final clean poster composition: open-to-closed trap sequence around two amber pulses, AION small at edge with cyan crystal signature.
